stem:
Dhruv stands on soft soil in flat sandals. He then stands on the same soil in narrow-heeled shoes. His weight is the same in both cases.

Which statement about the pressure on the soil is correct?

options.text: The pressure is greater in the narrow heels, because the same force acts on a smaller contact area.
The pressure is smaller in the narrow heels, because a smaller contact area always lowers pressure.
The pressure is the same in both cases, because his weight does not change.
The pressure is greater in the flat sandals, because the flat sandals cover more soft soil.

teacher.key_rationale: At the same perpendicular force, pressure rises when contact area falls. Narrow heels have smaller area, so greater pressure. B reverses the area–pressure link. C ignores area. D judges from how much soil is covered without the force-per-area rule.
